data.name: Kaynat
data.gender_notes: Kaynat is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Kaynat means the one who gives or distributes, often used metaphorically for a benevolent and generous person. This name is rooted in the rich tradition of Islamic spirituality and kindness. The name Kaynat carries the meaning “The giver or distributor” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kaynat usually hope their child will grow to embody the giver or distributor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of generosity and giving in the Islamic tradition.
data.etymology: Kaynat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The giver or distributor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kaynat total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: كَيْنَات
in_arabic.long_meaning: كَيْنَات: مُصَنّف في علم الكلام، يعد اسمًا من أسماء الله الحسنى، ذُكر في القرآن الكريم في سورة الأعراف، آية 190، يُستخدم في علم التفسير، ويُستشهد به في حديث النبي محمد، يُعتبر اسمًا من أسماء الله الحسنى، ويعني "الذي يخلق" أو "الخالق"

in_urdu.name: کینات

in_english.name: Kaynat
in_english.meaning: Creator, Originator, One who brings to life
in_english.long_meaning: Kaynat is an Islamic name that refers to Allah as the Creator, Originator, and One who brings to life. The name Kaynat is mentioned in the Quran in Surah Al-A'raf, verse 190, and is used in Islamic theology to describe Allah's role in creating life. The name Kaynat is also used in Islamic tradition to refer to Allah's power to create and sustain life. It is a beautiful and meaningful name that reflects the Islamic concept of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of the universe.
